text.text_excerpt: Another great place for local, live New Orleans music every night of the week. There's a $5 cover on the weekends, but free the rest of the week. It's got a prime location right in the heart of Frenchman Street so there are many other music venues close by to hop around to. There's a huge beer selection, but it's a little pricier then everywhere else around. I think this location is related to the d.b.a. in NYC so it has a sleeker more swanky look to it. The bar split nicely with one side dedicated to music and dancing, the other side has tables, and there's a small back room with couches. It's much larger than all the other venues on Frenchman. d.b.a. is definitely worth checking out. Th...

This *might* be my favorite venue on Frenchmen Street, although, I didn't go to one that I disliked. d.b.a. has a bar with a stage and dance floor on one side and a space with just a bar and some seating on the other: so there's a place to be close to the action and hear live music, and a space where you can just chat and hear the live jazz in the background. My friend and I came here on a Saturday and Sunday and on both nights the music was great and it wasn't terribly crowded (although we were here on the early side: 8:30pm). Service was a little slow, but that's a minor offense. I'll be back the next time I find myself in New Orleans.

I REALLY liked this place. Our bartender from Desire's on Bourbon St. told us if we want to avoid the drunk frat boys and marines to get off Bourbon and head down to Frenchman St. specifically to go to a jazz bar called d.b.a. About 9 blocks down, walking through some beautiful neighborhoods, we emerged from Bourbon on to a new type of setting. More folks on the porch, locals, musicians, no loud drunk A&F bro's walking around, no girls stumbling in high heels with their hurricane drinks (though 5 years ago I'd have preffered that. ) We arrived dba, which is across the st from a place called "the spotted cat" also another jazz bar.
